class.name: TickNetwork
class.brief_description: Tick based network: server authority, client prediction and interpolation.
class.description: Synchronizes the [TickObject] nodes over a [TickTransport], in fixed ticks. The peer with id 1 is the server: it simulates every object, moving each one with the input of its controller. A client predicts the objects it controls and rewinds them when the server disagrees; the other objects are interpolated [member interpolation_delay] seconds behind the server. The network ticks during the physics process; set [member ticks_per_second] equal to [member ProjectSettings.physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second], so bodies moved with the physics delta (like [method CharacterBody3D.move_and_slide]) advance one tick at a time. The client uses the server's tick rate. The client's clock is synchronized with the server's, and the client runs ahead of the server just enough for its inputs to arrive in time, adapting its speed to the network conditions.

method.name: get_event_frame
method.description: Returns the frame [param seconds] after the current one. To run an event at the same frame on every peer, the server sends it for a frame far enough ahead to cover the latency, for example [code]get_event_frame(0.5)[/code].

method.name: get_frame
method.description: Returns the next frame to simulate. Clients run ahead of the server.

method.name: get_local_peer_id
method.description: Returns the id of this peer in the transport, or 0 when not running.

method.name: get_rtt
method.description: Returns the round trip time to the server, in seconds, as measured by the clock synchronization (client only).

method.name: get_stats
method.description: Returns a [Dictionary] with statistics: [code]rewinds[/code], [code]rewound_frames[/code], [code]ghost_inputs[/code] (inputs repeated by the server because they were missing), [code]late_inputs[/code], [code]rejected_inputs[/code], [code]full_snapshots_sent[/code], [code]delta_snapshots_sent[/code], [code]snapshots_received[/code], [code]snapshots_dropped[/code], [code]malformed_packets[/code], [code]rate_limited_packets[/code], [code]events_sent[/code], [code]events_received[/code], [code]events_rejected[/code], [code]spawns[/code], [code]despawns[/code], [code]time_scale[/code] (the client's speed adjustment), [code]timeline_frame[/code] (this peer's estimate of the authority's current frame, negative while unknown), [code]latest_snapshot_frame[/code], and for dolls (see [member TickObject.remote_mode]): [code]doll_rewinds[/code], [code]doll_rewound_frames[/code], [code]doll_corrections[/code], [code]doll_resyncs[/code], [code]doll_ghost_inputs[/code] and [code]doll_delays[/code] (a [Dictionary] with how many frames the dolls of each peer are behind this peer's timeline). With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: [code]states_sent[/code], [code]states_received[/code], [code]stale_states[/code], [code]malformed_packets[/code], [code]transfers[/code], [code]orphans[/code], [code]denied_requests[/code], [code]events_sent[/code], [code]events_received[/code], [code]events_forwarded[/code], [code]events_rejected[/code], [code]spawns[/code], [code]despawns[/code] and [code]timeline_frame[/code].

method.name: get_transport
method.description: Returns the transport passed to [method start].

method.name: is_predicting
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] on a client once its clock is synchronized and it predicts its objects.

method.name: is_rewinding
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while a client simulates again past frames after a correction. Use it to skip side effects (sounds, particles) during the rewind.

method.name: is_server
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this peer is the server.

method.name: send_event
method.description: Sends an event without target object, received with [signal event_received]. From a client, it goes to the server, for [param frame] (by default, the frame the client predicts). From the server, it goes to [param peer], or every client with 0, and runs on arrival or, with [param frame], when the client's simulation reaches that frame. The [param payload] can't contain objects and is limited to [member max_event_size] bytes. Events aren't repeated during rewinds.

method.name: start
method.description: Starts the network over [param transport]. The peer with id 1 becomes the server; the others are clients and join when connected to it.

method.name: stop
method.description: Stops the network. The objects stay registered and synchronize again on the next [method start].

members.member: [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE]: one peer ([member authority_peer]) simulates every object — the server of a star, or one node of a mesh. [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: every object has an owner node that simulates it and sends its state to the other nodes, and ownership can change (see [method TickObject.request_authority]); for trusted meshes of servers, without prediction.

With [constant AUTHORITY_SINGLE]: the peer that simulates every object, is the destination of inputs and events, and is the clock master — the hub of a star (1), or the node of a mesh chosen by the project.
With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: the node whose timeline the others follow.

Another [TickNetwork] of this process whose timeline this one follows (only for the [member authority_peer] of this network). A game server's star with its clients follows the cluster's network, so the clients, the game server and the cluster's authority use the same frames. Place the followed network before this one in the tree.

Called on the server as [code]validator(sender: int, event: StringName, payload: Variant) -> bool[/code] for each event without target object sent by a client; returning [code]false[/code] refuses it. Without a validator, those events are accepted.
Frames of history kept for snapshots, predictions and interpolation.
Number of past inputs repeated in each input packet, against packet loss.

If [code]false[/code], the objects this peer doesn't simulate get the state of the latest snapshot without interpolation. Use it on game servers that relay a cluster's objects to their own clients, so only the final clients interpolate.
How far behind the server, in seconds, the interpolated objects are rendered.
With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: owners send the state of every object at least every [member keyframe_interval] ticks, even if it didn't change; in between, only the objects that changed.
Largest event payload, in bytes. With [constant TRUST_UNTRUSTED], larger events from clients are refused.
With [constant TRUST_UNTRUSTED], the events each client can send per second (with a burst of the same size); the excess is dropped.
Largest number of inputs the client tries to keep buffered on the server.
Smallest number of inputs the client tries to keep buffered on the server; more jitter increases it up to [member max_input_buffer].

With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: the node that keeps the registry of owners. Every change of owner goes through it and increases the object's version; state with an older version is discarded. Choose a node that stays up: the registry isn't replaced if it leaves.
Node the paths of the objects are relative to. The same object must have the same path on every peer.
The server sends a snapshot every [member snapshot_interval] ticks.
Ticks per second of the simulation. Clients use the server's value.

How much the server trusts the clients. With [constant TRUST_UNTRUSTED], it limits the rate and size of what they send, and accepts an event for an object only from its controller unless [method TickObject._validate_event] decides. The input of an object is always taken only from its controller, and state only from the server.

signal.name: authority_changed
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted on every node when the owner of [param object] changes ([param new_owner] is 0 when nobody owns it).

signal.name: authority_orphaned
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted on every node when the owner of [param object] left (or released it to nobody). Nobody simulates it until the project assigns it, for example with [method TickObject.assign_authority]. [param last_frame] is the frame of its last known state.

signal.name: authority_request_denied
signal.description: With [constant AUTHORITY_DISTRIBUTED]: emitted when a request for [param object] is refused: another transfer of it was in progress, or its owner refused it.

signal.name: event_received
signal.description: Emitted when an event without target object runs: on the server for events from clients, on clients for events from the server ([param sender] is 1). [param frame] is the frame the event was sent for.

signal.name: peer_left
signal.description: Emitted when a client leaves (on the server) or when the connection with the server is lost (on a client).

signal.name: peer_ready
signal.description: Emitted on the server when a client passes the handshake, and on a client when the server accepts it ([param peer] is 1).

signal.name: prediction_started
signal.description: Emitted on a client when its clock is synchronized and it starts predicting its objects.

signal.name: rejected
signal.description: Emitted on a client when the server refuses it, for example because of a different protocol version or precision build.

signal.name: rewound
signal.description: Emitted on a client after a rewind: the predicted objects diverged from the server at [param frame], and [param frame_count] frames were simulated again.

constants.constant: The clients may be modified or malicious: the server limits and validates what they send. The default.
The peers are trusted (for example, servers of the same cluster): no rate or size limits, and events are accepted from any peer.
Every object has an owner node, and ownership can change.
